title: LeBron James Makes His Title Intentions Clear at 76ers Media Day
htmlContent:
For the first time,LeBron James stood in front of reporters wearing a Philadelphia 76ers jersey. At the team's media day on Monday, the four-time champion covered everything from why he picked Philadelphia to what role he expects to play, and he left little doubt about the standard he's setting for his new team.

"I didn't leave my family to lose in the second round," James said.

Why Philadelphia

James revealed that his list of potential destinations had been narrowed to five teams, with the Sixers among the finalists. What pushed Philadelphia over the top, he said, was largely Tyrese Maxey.

The two spoke several times during James' decision-making process, and James said he used those talks to ask Maxey every question he could think of. When he broke down each franchise he was weighing, James said, his relationship with the Sixers guard emerged as one of the main factors in his choice.

Early Impressions of His New Team

Asked what he has learned in the weeks since signing, James said the biggest takeaway has been alignment. In his view, the front office, coaching staff and players all share the same vision for where the franchise is headed, and everyone is willing to put in the work to get there. That shared commitment, he said, matters more than anything else.

James was also asked whether this could be the final contract of his career. He declined to look that far down the road, saying he is taking things one day at a time and staying focused on the present.

A Role With No Limits

When the conversation turned to his role, James initially gave a team-first answer, saying he'll do whatever the Sixers need from him. Then he paused and made a bolder point: the beauty of his game, he said, is that he can handle any responsibility on the floor.

"Literally, I can do everything," he added.

Patience Over 'Instant Oatmeal'

For all his championship talk, James was careful to temper expectations about how quickly things will come together. He compared today's demand for immediate results to instant oatmeal, arguing that anything special requires time and daily commitment to work that isn't always enjoyable.

His message to his new teammates centered on embracing discomfort. James said the fastest way for a group to become great is to get comfortable being uncomfortable and, ideally, to learn to love that grind. If the Sixers can buy into that mindset, he believes they can become a great team.

From Rival to Hometown Favorite

James also reflected on his history with Philadelphia fans, who have spent years rooting against him. He described that relationship as one built on hostility but underpinned by mutual respect, and said he enjoyed the boos as much as anyone. Now, he noted, the two sides are finally on the same team.

Still, he joked that he hopes a few fans keep giving him a hard time, explaining that he feeds off that kind of tension and needs it to stay sharp.

What's Next

The Sixers won't have to wait long for a major test. Philadelphia opens the 2026–27 season on Tuesday, Oct. 20, on the road against the reigning NBA champion New York Knicks, an early measuring stick for a team that, by James' own standard, is aiming far higher than a second-round exit.
excerpt: At his first Philadelphia 76ers media day, LeBron James made clear he joined the franchise to compete for a championship, citing Tyrese Maxey as a key factor in his decision and setting a standard far beyond a second-round exit.
